title: Each evidence option fits one reading
statement: In a two-part item asking for evidence behind the first answer, only the keyed evidence may support the right answer, and each wrong evidence option should fit a wrong reading.
detail: Two-part evidence items came into the evaluator with mandatory copy-task audits of how the evidence part links to the answer part (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/ebsr_evaluation.txt`). An item fails when an evidence option is not drawn from the passage or when a wrong evidence option also supports the keyed answer, and each wrong evidence option must align to a wrong reading of the first part, not to the key. When a test-wise student can pick the evidence through a surface cue without doing the first part, the item measures test-wiseness instead of evidence-based reasoning; mixing quotations with paraphrases among the evidence options is failed as an unintended cue.
against: The evaluator's text-hidden probe does not cover this item type: 'ebsr/match/sequence/saq/scr reported not-probeable (v1 scope).' (`shadow-bench`, git commit e435432, line 14).

evidence.quote: - a Part B option has `appears_in_passage: NO` (evidence is fabricated, not drawn from the passage);
- a NON-keyed Part B option has `supports_part_a_keyed_answer: YES` (a distractor is itself valid supporting evidence, so the Part B key is not the unique/complete set).
Each Part B distractor must align to a WRONG Part A reading, not to the key.

When a test-wise student can pick the evidence without performing the Part A comprehension, the item no longer measures evidence-based reasoning — it measures test-wiseness, defeating the EBSR purpose.
mixing quotes and paraphrases turns citation style into an unintended cue
- **No vocabulary EBSR or hot-text:** Vocabulary items use short context sentences as stimulus, not full passages. Two-part text-evidence format does not apply.
